title.narrative: Countering Opaque Negotiations and Confidentiality in PRC’s External Agreements and Lending (CONCEAL)

description.narrative: Through a dual approach of evidence generation and targeted advocacy at both national and global levels, the project aims to counter the use of confidentiality clauses in borrowing agreements by China, and others lenders such as the Islamic Development Bank and France. By strengthening domestic transparency, TI seeks to reduce opportunities for corruption in debt acquisition and management. The project will draw on a set of case studies from countries currently at risk of debt distress: Malawi, Sri Lanka and Venezuela. These case studies will highlight China’s and other creditors’ hidden debt practices across different governance, economic, and strategic contexts. Building on this evidence, the project will implement a global advocacy strategy to influence reforms while simultaneously supporting national-level efforts to limit the use of confidentiality clauses in lending agreements. Value of the contract is USD 250,000

recipient-country.narrative: This project is managed by TI-S which is headquartered in Germany. The countries involved are Malawi, Sri Lanka, Venezuela, and the US
